<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="transcriber" />{{RunningHeader|950|TIDE|}}</noinclude>equilibrium tide <math>\epsilon</math>, which is as we know equal to <math>E_2P_2\cos(2nft+\alpha)</math>. Whence we find
{{block center|<math>\mathbf{b} = -\frac{3b_2\gamma}{4ma}\frac{\epsilon}{P_2}\{3\cdot5K_2P_2+3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot9K_2K_4P_4+3\cdot5\dots13K_2K_4K_6P_6\dots\}</math>.}}

{{smaller block|The number <math>f</math> is a fraction such that its reciprocal is twice the number of sidereal days in the period of the tide. The greatest value of <math>f</math> is that appertaining to the lunar fortnightly tide (Mf in notation of harmonic analysis), and in this case <math>f</math> is in round numbers 1/28, or more exactly <math>f^2 = \cdot00133</math>. The ratio of the density <math>\sigma</math> of sea-water to <math>\delta</math> the mean density of the earth is ·18093; which value gives us
{{block center|<math>b_2 = 1-\frac{3\sigma}{5\delta} = \cdot89144</math>.}}
The quantity <math>m</math> is the ratio of equatorial centrifugal force to gravity, and is equal to 1/289. Finally, <math>\gamma/a</math> is the depth of the ocean expressed as a fraction of the earth's radius.}}

With these numerical values Mr Hough has applied the solution to determine the lunar fortnightly tide for oceans of various depths. Of his results we give two:—

''First'', when <math>\gamma = 7260</math> ft. = 1210 fathoms, which makes <math>\gamma/4ma = 1/40</math>, he finds
{{block center|<math>\mathbf{b} = \frac{\epsilon}{P_2}\{\cdot2669P_2-\cdot1678P_4+\cdot0485P_6-\cdot0081P_8+\cdot0009P_{10}-\cdot0001P_{12}\dots\}</math>.}}
If the equilibrium theory were true we should have
{{block center|<math>\mathbf{b} = \frac{\epsilon}{P_2}\{P_2\}</math>;}}
thus we see how widely the dynamical solution differs from the equilibrium value.

''Secondly'', when <math>\gamma = 58080</math> ft. = 9680 fathoms, and <math>\gamma/4ma = 1/5</math>, he finds
{{block center|<math>\mathbf{b} = \frac{\epsilon}{P_2}\{\cdot7208P_2-\cdot0973P_4+\cdot0048P_6-\cdot0001P_8\dots\}</math>.}}

{{smaller block|From this we see that the equilibrium solution presents some sort of approximation to the dynamical one; and it is clear that the equilibrium solution would be fairly accurate for oceans which are still quite shallow when expressed as fractions of the earth's radius, although far deeper than the actual sea.}}

{{smaller block|The tides of long period were not investigated by Laplace in this manner, for he was of opinion that a very small amount of friction would suffice to make the ocean assume its form of equilibrium. In the arguments which he adduced in support of this view the friction contemplated was such that the integral effect was proportional to the velocity of the water relatively to the bottom. It is probable that proportionality to the square of the velocity would have been nearer the truth, but the distinction is unimportant.}}

{{smaller block|The most rapid of the oscillations of this class is the lunar fortnightly tide, and the water of the ocean moves northward for a week and then southward for a week. In oscillating systems, where the resistances are proportional to the velocities, it is usual to specify the resistance by a "modulus of decay," namely the time in which a velocity is reduced by friction to <math>e^{-1}</math> or 1/2·78 of its initial value. Now in order that the result contemplated by Laplace may be true, the friction must be such that the modulus of decay is short compared with the semi-period of oscillation. It seems certain that the friction of the ocean bed would not reduce a slow ocean current to one-third of its primitive value in a day or two. Hence we cannot accept Laplace's discussion as satisfactory, and the investigation which has just been given becomes necessary. (See § 34).}}

{{smaller block|§ 18. ''Tesseral Oscillations''.—The oscillations which we now have to consider are those in which the form of surface is
{{EB1911 Shoulder Heading|Transformation of Equation.}}
expressible by the tesseral harmonics. The results will be applicable to the diurnal and semi-diurnal tides—Laplace's second and third species.}}

If we write <math>\sigma = s/f</math> the equation (22) becomes
{{block center|<math>\frac{d}{d\theta}\left[\frac{\left(\sin\theta\frac{d}{d\theta}+\sigma\cos\theta\right)\Sigma b_iu_i}{s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta}\right] - \frac{\left(\sigma\cos\theta\frac{d}{d\theta}+s^2\operatorname{cosec}\theta\right)\Sigma b_iu_i}{s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta}</math>}}
{{block center|<math>+\frac{4ma}{\gamma\sigma^2}\sin\theta\Sigma h_i = 0</math>. (29)}}
If we write <math>D</math> for the operation <math>\sin\theta\frac{d}{d\theta}</math>, the middle term may be arranged in the form
{{block center|<math>-\frac{\sigma\cot\theta\,(D+\sigma\cos\theta)(\Sigma b_iu_i)}{s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta} - \frac{\Sigma b_iu_i}{\sin\theta}</math>.}}
Therefore on multiplying by <math>\sin\theta</math> the equation becomes
{{block center|<math>(D-\sigma\cos\theta)\left[\frac{(D+\sigma\cos\theta)(\Sigma b_iu_i)}{s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta}\right] - (\Sigma b_iu_i) + \frac{4ma}{\gamma\sigma^2}\sin^2\theta\Sigma h_i = 0</math>. (30)}}

{{smaller block|We now introduce two auxiliary functions, such that
{{block center|<math>\Sigma b_i(h_i-e_i) = \Sigma b_iu_i</math>}}
{{block center|<math>= (D-\sigma\cos\theta)\Psi+(s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta)\Phi</math>. (31)}}
It is easy to prove that
{{block center|<math>\left.\begin{array}{l}(D+\sigma\cos\theta)(D-\sigma\cos\theta) = D^2-s^2+\sigma\sin^2\theta+(s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta),\\(D-\sigma\cos\theta)(D+\sigma\cos\theta) = D^2-s^2-\sigma\sin^2\theta+(s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta).\end{array}\right\}</math>. (32)}} Also
{{block center|<math>(D+\sigma\cos\theta)(s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta)\,\Phi=(s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta)(D+\sigma\cos\theta)\Phi</math>}}
{{block center|<math>+2\sigma^2\sin^2\theta\cos\theta\,\Phi.</math> (33)}}
Now perform <math>\text{D}+\sigma\cos\theta</math> on (31), and use the first of (32) and (33), and we have
{{block center|<math>(D+\sigma\cos\theta)(\Sigma b_iu_i)=(D^2-s^2+\sigma\sin^2\theta+s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta)\Psi.</math>}}
{{block center|<math>+(s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta)(D+\sigma\cos\theta)\Phi+2\sigma^2\sin^2\theta\cos\theta\,\Phi.</math> (34)}}}}

{{smaller block|The functions <math>\Psi</math> and <math>\Phi</math> are as yet indeterminate, and we may impose another condition on them. Let that condition be
{{block center|<math>(D^2-s^2+\sigma\sin^2\theta)\Psi=-2\sigma^2\sin^2\theta\cos\theta\,\Phi.</math> (35)}}
Then (34) may be written
{{block center|<math>\frac{(D+\sigma\cos\theta)(\Sigma b_iu_i)}{s^2-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta}=\Psi+(D+\sigma\cos\theta)\Phi.</math>}}}}

Substituting from this in (30), and using the second of (32), the function <math>\Psi</math> disappears and the equation reduces to
{{block center|<math>(D^2-s^2-\sigma\sin^2\theta)\Phi+\frac{4ma}{\gamma\sigma^2}\sin^2\theta\,\Sigma h_i=0.</math> (36)}}

Since by (35) <math>-\sigma^2\cos^2\theta\,\Phi=\tfrac{1}{2}\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}(D^2-s^2+\sigma\sin^2\theta)\Psi</math>, (31) may be written
{{block center|<math>\Sigma b_iu_i=\left[D-\sigma\cos\theta+\tfrac{1}{2}\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}(D^2-s^2+\sigma\sin^2\theta)\right]\Psi+s^2\Phi.</math> (37)}}

{{smaller block|The equations (35), (36) and (37) define <math>\Psi</math> and <math>\Phi</math>, and furnish the equation which must be satisfied.}}

If we denote <math>\cos\theta</math> by <math>\mu</math> the zonal harmonics are defined by
{{block center|<math>P_i=\frac{1}{2^ii!}\left(\frac{d}{d\mu}\right)^i(\mu^2-1)^i.</math>}}

The following are three well-known properties of zonal harmonics:
{{block center|<math>\frac{d}{d\mu}\left[(1-\mu^2)\frac{dP_i}{d\mu}\right]+i(i+1)P_i=0,</math> (38)}}
{{block center|<math>(i+1)P_{i+1}-(2i+1)\mu P_i+iP_{i-1}=0,</math> (39)}}
{{block center|<math>\frac{dP_{i+1}}{d\mu}-\frac{dP_{i-1}}{d\mu}=(2i+1)P_i.</math> (40)}}

If <math>P^s_i\begin{smallmatrix}\cos\\ \sin\end{smallmatrix}s\phi</math> are the two tesseral harmonics of order <math>i</math> and rank <math>s</math>, it is also known that
{{block center|<math>P^s_i=(1-\mu^2)^{\frac{1}{2}s}\frac{d^sP_i}{d\mu^s}.</math> (41)}}

Let us now assume
{{block center|<math>h_i=C^s_iP^s_i,\quad e_i=E^s_iP^s_i,\quad \Psi=\Sigma\alpha^s_iP^s_i,\quad \Phi=\Sigma\beta^s_iP^s_i.</math>}}

{{smaller block|These must now be substituted in our three equations (35), (36), (37), and the result must be expressed by series of the <math>P^s_i</math> functions. It is clear then that we have to transform into <math>P^s_i</math> functions the following functions of <math>P^s_i</math>, namely
{{block center|<math>\frac{1}{\sin^2\theta}(D^2-s^2\pm\sigma\sin^2\theta)P^s_i,\quad \cos\theta P^s_i,</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\left[D-\sigma\cos\theta+\tfrac{1}{2}\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}(D^2-s^2+\sigma\sin^2\theta)\right]P^s_i.</math>}}}}

If we differentiate (38) <math>s</math> times, and express the result by means of the operator <math>D</math>, we find
{{block center|<math>(D^2-s^2)P^s_i+i(i+1)P^s_i\sin^2\theta=0.</math> (42)}}

Again, differentiating (39) <math>s</math> times and using (40), we find
{{block center|<math>(i-s+1)P^s_{i+1}-(2i+1)\cos\theta\,P^s_i+(i+s)P^s_{i-1}=0.</math> (43)}}

Lastly, differentiating (41) once and using (38), (40) and (43)
{{block center|<math>DP^s_i=\frac{i(i-s+1)}{2i+1}P^s_{i+1}-\frac{(i+1)(i+s)}{2i+1}P^s_{i-1}.</math> (44)}}

By means of (42), (43) and (44) we have
{{block center|<math>\frac{1}{\sin^2\theta}(D^2-s^2\pm\sigma\sin^2\theta)P^s_i=[-i(i+1)\pm\sigma]P^s_i,</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\cos\theta\,P^s_i=\frac{i+s}{2i+1}P^s_{i-1}+\frac{i-s+1}{2i+1}P^s_{i+1},</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\left[D-\sigma+\tfrac{1}{2}\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}(D^2-s^2+\sigma\sin^2\theta)\right]P^s_i=-\frac{(i-s+1)[\sigma+i(i-1)]}{2(2i+1)}P^s_{i+1}</math>}}
{{block center|<math>-\frac{(i+s)[\sigma+(i+1)(i+2)]}{2(2i+1)}P^s_{i-1}.</math>}}

Therefore the equations (35), (36), (37) give
{{block center|<math>\Sigma\left[\alpha^s_i\{-i(i+1)+\sigma\}P^s_i+2\sigma^2\beta^s_i\left\{\frac{i+s}{2i+1}P^s_{i-1}+\frac{i-s+1}{2i+1}P^s_{i+1}\right\}\right]=0,</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\Sigma\left[\beta^s_i\{-i(i+1)-\sigma\}P^s_i+\frac{4ma}{\gamma\sigma^2}C^s_iP^s_i\right]=0,</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\Sigma\left[b_i(C^s_i-E^s_i)P^s_i+\alpha^s_i\left\{\frac{(i-s+1)[\sigma+i(i-1)]}{2(2i+1}P^s_{i+1}\right.\right.</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\left.\left.+\frac{(i+s)[\sigma+(i+1)(i+2)]}{2(2i+1)}P^s_{i-1}\right\}-\beta^s_is^2P^s_i\right]=0.</math>}}<noinclude><references/></noinclude>
